kind: declared measurement change — the decision column gains a quantum band; filed BEFORE any v3.1 statistic runs, not discovered in a delta table
subject: the QMA vocabulary gap surfaced by the Complexity Garden screen
note: Owner ruling 2026-07-24: the Garden's QMA-complete problems are admissible-but-unexpressible, the same defect class as the SVP/CVP sum-of-radicals gap (clarification-02). Resolved by EXTENDING the decision vocabulary, not forcing a wrong rung. Same shape as superpoly-APX and ruled the same way. This note records the CONSEQUENCE for the battery before any v3.1 decision-column statistic is computed.

change.vocabulary: The decision charge gains TWO completeness rungs and ONE membership value: `QMA-complete`, `QMA1-complete` (ASCII for QMA_1, perfect completeness), and `in-QMA`. TWO rungs, not one, because the theorems draw the distinction: quantum-2-SAT is in P while quantum-k-SAT (k>=3) is QMA_1-complete (a permanent/determinant-style near-surface reversal), and QMA_1 is the class the quantum-k-SAT theorem proves completeness for. Collapsing QMA_1 into QMA would blur a cited distinction. The rung count follows the theorems, not parsimony.
change.ordinal_coding: The decision column's ordinal GAINS TWO LEVELS (7 rungs -> 9 completeness positions; kernel/v2 stays at 7 by construction). Placement: NP subset QMA_1 subset QMA subset PSPACE, so both quantum rungs sit ABOVE NPC and BELOW PSPACE-complete. Partial order edges added: (NPC, QMA1-complete), (QMA1-complete, QMA-complete), (QMA-complete, PSPACE-complete), (in-QMA, QMA-complete). INCOMPARABILITY to the PH rungs (PH-complete, coNP-complete) is recorded as a NON-edge here, not forced into the ordering -- the same convention that placed superpoly-APX.
change.membership_value: `in-QMA` is a MEMBERSHIP value, the quantum analogue of `NPI-candidate`. group-non-membership is IN QMA (Watrous, FOCS 2000), not known QMA-complete. It is admitted because the PLACEMENT ITSELF IS THE THEOREM -- the same bar factoring and graph-isomorphism clear as NPI-candidates on NP-intersect-coAM-style evidence. Watrous's 'in QMA, not known in MA' is that evidence's quantum form. The value is recorded as membership, NEVER dressed as completeness, exactly as NPI-candidate rows never claim hardness.
change.affected_statistics: any v2-vs-v3.1 comparison whose estimator consumes the decision column as an ordered/nominal factor: decision-column occupancy, the factors indicator matrix (widens in V3_SPEC only), any decision-stratified gradient. B3 (NPI calibration) is unaffected -- in-QMA is a distinct value, not an NPI-candidate.

handling.rule: both-values-always -- every decision-column table reports the v2 value and the v3 value side by side; any decision-column comparison carries the coding-change flag.
handling.requirement: Where a v2-vs-v3.1 decision-column delta is reported, it MUST be accompanied by a re-run under the v2 7-rung coding (to_v2_coding collapses QMA/QMA1/in-QMA to their nearest v2-expressible bound, PSPACE-complete, since QMA subset PSPACE) so the reader separates INSTRUMENT change from POPULATION change. Same discipline as clarification-02's approximation dual-coding.
handling.scope: The rungs are implemented in V3_SPEC ONLY (dev/quarry_v3_spec.py), never the kernel charges.py. THE VOCABULARY IS PART OF THE INSTRUMENT -- a kernel edit would perturb the v2 factors indicator matrix and confound the very comparison this note protects (clarification-02's lesson, instance 8).
